title: Director, Stakeholder Engagement, Congress Strategy & Operations, Congresses
text:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

**The Opportunity:**

As part of our expanding Medical Affairs organization, we seek a dynamic and experienced Director, Stakeholder Engagement Strategy & Operations to support the strategy, planning, and execution of global medical congress activitiesand elevate Revolution Medicines’ presence at major scientific congresses as our portfolio and organization grow. This individual will report to the Head of Scientific Stakeholder Engagement within Global Medical Excellence and will partner cross-functionally with Commercial, Clinical Development, and Research, providing leadership for global congress activities to ensure seamless integration of congress objectives with broader organizational priorities. Key responsibilities will include:

Congress Strategy & Execution

* Develop congress strategy for Medical Affairs with a focus on oncology therapeutic areas including pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal cancer.
* Lead the strategy to elevate Revolution Medicines’ presence at major global scientific congresses, building a best-in-class congress model that expands our scientific visibility, stakeholder engagement, and impact as the company and portfolio grow.
* Drive development of strategic objectives, overall congress presence, scientific messaging, and engagement plans.
* Ensure high-quality, compliant execution of congress activities including medical booths, satellite events, and onsite pre-congress meetings.
* Lead Medical Affairs planning for global congresses in the U.S., EU, and APAC regions, ensuring global consistency with regional adaptation.
* Assess evolving needs and establish digital capabilities and processes to deliver timely, congress-specific scientific content to external stakeholders while ensuring appropriate governance and compliance across global markets.
* Evaluate and shape congress key performance indicators (KPIs) to optimize approach, priorities, and investments.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

* Partner with Commercial, Clinical Development, and Research to ensure consistent communication and scientific engagement while maintaining appropriate governance and firewalls.
* Act as the central coordination point for cross-functional teams to align on congress priorities, deliverables, and messaging.
* Collaborate with Publications/Medical Communications to ensure alignment of abstracts, posters, oral presentations, and key data dissemination to other congress activities.

Operational Leadership & Governance

* Provide strategic direction and oversight to agency and vendor partners across congress activities, including booth development, ancillary events, internal meetings, and external stakeholder receptions, with accountability for budgets, timelines, operational excellence, and global and regional compliance.
* Ensure compliance with global and regional regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, PMDA, EFPIA, IFPMA).
* Establish best practices, SOPs, and governance processes for global congress planning.
* Capture and disseminate post-congress insights in collaboration with Medical Affairs Insights & Analytics and the broader Medical Affairs group.

**Required Skills, Experience and Education:**

* Advanced degree (MS, PharmD, PhD or equivalent in life sciences preferred but not required).
* 10+ years’ experience in Medical Affairs within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry, preferably within a large, global pharmaceutical organization, with significant oncology experience and a strong background in congress strategy.
* Demonstrated experience leading congress strategy at scale within a global pharmaceutical or biotechnology organization, with a track record of building high-impact, integrated scientific congress presence across multiple functions, programs, and geographies.
* Strong understanding of oncology therapeutic landscape, particularly pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and colorectal cancer.
* Deep knowledge of compliance standards governing global congresses and scientific exchange.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional collaboration in a complex, matrixed environment.
* Excellent project management, organizational, and communication skills.
* Experience managing budgets, vendors, and operational processes related to congresses.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Experience in early and late-phase development and product launch preparation in oncology.
* Understanding of global medical congress operations and digital engagement tools.
* Experience working in fast-paced, innovative, clinical-stage biotech organizations.
